page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the arm64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by Ampere AmpereOne processors running at a constant base clock of 3.0 GHz. With a single thread per physical core, the instance ensures that each vCPU operates without thread contention from simultaneous multithreading. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, meaning persistent storage requirements must be fulfilled via network-attached block volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default. Because the instance pairs 16 dedicated cores with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it prioritizes processing density over memory capacity, delivering predictable compute execution per allocated core across sustained execution windows.

With its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio and dedicated AmpereOne compute cores, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-32 is tailored for workloads that require linear scaling without high memory footprints. Well-suited workloads include distributed build runners, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, containerized application microservices, batch compute jobs, and web serving clusters compiled for 64-bit Arm architectures.
